title: You can apply for an H-4 EAD
ask: Your spouse's I-140 is approved, which makes you eligible for an H-4 EAD (Form I-765, category (c)(26)). Have you applied?
why: The EAD lets you work for any employer. It is valid only as long as your H-4 I-94, so file it together with every H-4 extension.

title: On H-4 without an EAD
ask: Are you sure nothing you do counts as work: no freelancing, no paid remote work for an Indian company, no monetised content, no trading run as a business?
why: Work without authorisation is a status violation that can surface years later at the I-485 stage. Volunteering and study are fine.

title: Your I-94 expires within 6 months
ask: Is your I-539 (and your children's) being filed together with your spouse's H-1B extension, plus the I-765 renewal if you have an EAD?
why: H-4 status does not extend automatically with the H-1B. Filing together keeps the decisions in step and avoids a gap in work authorisation.

title: Travelling with a pending I-539
ask: Do you know that leaving the US while your I-539 extension or change of status is pending abandons it?
why: You can re-enter on a valid H-4 visa stamp and receive a new I-94, but the pending application is treated as abandoned and may need to be refiled.

title: On H-4 without an EAD
ask: Do you have an ITIN so your spouse can file a joint tax return with you on it?
why: Without an SSN you need an ITIN (Form W-7) to appear on a joint return, which is usually worth a lot in tax.
